Problem Restatement

We are given the permutation

$$p=(1\,2\,5\,4)(2\,3)\in S_5.$$

Determine the index $[S_5:\langle p\rangle]$ of the cyclic subgroup $\langle p\rangle$ generated by $p$ in the symmetric group $S_5$.

Definitions and Known Results

1. Symmetric group: $S_5$ is the group of all permutations of the set $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$. Its order is $|S_5|=5!=120$.

2. Composition convention: For permutations written as products, the rightmost factor is applied first. Thus for each $x\in\{1,\dots,5\}$,
$$p(x)=(1\,2\,5\,4)\big((2\,3)(x)\big).$$

3. Order of a permutation: The order of a permutation equals the least common multiple (lcm) of the lengths of the cycles in its disjoint-cycle decomposition. In particular, a $k$-cycle has order $k$.

4. Index formula: If $H$ is a subgroup of a finite group $G$, then the index is

$$[G:H]=\frac{|G|}{|H|}.$$

Proof

We compute the action of $p$ on each element $1,2,3,4,5$ by applying $(2\,3)$ first and then $(1\,2\,5\,4)$.

- For $1$: $(2\,3)$ fixes $1$, so $(2\,3)(1)=1$. Then $(1\,2\,5\,4)$ sends $1\mapsto2$. Hence $p(1)=2$.

- For $2$: $(2\,3)$ sends $2\mapsto3$. Since $(1\,2\,5\,4)$ fixes $3$, we have $(1\,2\,5\,4)(3)=3$. Hence $p(2)=3$.

- For $3$: $(2\,3)$ sends $3\mapsto2$. Then $(1\,2\,5\,4)$ sends $2\mapsto5$. Hence $p(3)=5$.

- For $4$: $(2\,3)$ fixes $4$, so $(2\,3)(4)=4$. Then $(1\,2\,5\,4)$ sends $4\mapsto1$. Hence $p(4)=1$.

- For $5$: $(2\,3)$ fixes $5$, so $(2\,3)(5)=5$. Then $(1\,2\,5\,4)$ sends $5\mapsto4$. Hence $p(5)=4$.

From these images we follow the orbit starting at $1$:
$$1\mapsto2\mapsto3\mapsto5\mapsto4\mapsto1.$$

Thus the permutation $p$ is the 5-cycle

$$p=(1\,2\,3\,5\,4),$$

which is a single 5-cycle in disjoint-cycle form.

By definition of order of a permutation (item 3 above), the order of $p$ is the length of this cycle, namely $|p|=5$. Hence the cyclic subgroup generated by $p$ has cardinality

$$|\langle p\rangle|=5.$$

Applying the index formula (item 4) in the finite group $S_5$ of order 120, we obtain

$$[S_5:\langle p\rangle]=\frac{|S_5|}{|\langle p\rangle|}=\frac{120}{5}=24.$$

Final Conclusion

The index of $\langle p\rangle$ in $S_5$ is $[S_5:\langle p\rangle]=24$.
